newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle seen steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle seen steady to lower.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.150 cent per lb lower while feeder cattle were called steady to 0.100 cent lower, livestock analysts said.

Although boxed beef values continued to rise and post the highest price levels since early December, live cattle futures are seen under pressure as the market is showing topping action. Expectations were for August to rally up to 68 cents and that objective was reached earlier in the week, they said.
Back months also look technically weak after slipping back to near the 70-cent level, they said.

Feeder cattle futures were again expected to be influenced by trade in corn futures and higher indications there should weigh on feeders early. This will offset a small rise in the latest CME feeder cattle index and continued highest cash feeder prices since early 1994, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.08 at $82.46 per cwt.
